objective: Exhaustive census on small non-parity laws: every gluing of two three-place knots at one shared distinction, chains of three, and windows of the atom thread (a Horn law). For each pair of distinctions joined by a chain of knots, compare bond distance with chain distance counted in knots and in distinctions. A pair joined by a chain but by no common knot, or a chain whose union is smaller than every knot through its ends, is a law where the measures split; if one appears, build a uniform thread or plane from it and compare growth and circle shape.
status: Proved (BOND-CHAIN-20261108-001B-P001, exhaustive): of 1,156 laws of two three-place knots sharing one distinction, a knot joins the far ends exactly when they do not meet at a gate (72 gated laws, no such knot); chains of up to four single clauses are spanned by a knot exactly when they chain as implications; the NAND thread's only knots are its clauses.
title: Chains on laws that are not parity laws
